GuideWhatIsMoba.title: What Makes MOBAs So Addictive? A Deep Dive into 5v5 Battles
GuideWhatIsMoba.intro: I uninstalled my first MOBA the same night. Five years and 2,000 hours later, here is my attempt to work out why a 5v5 genre that loses you eight games in ten is so hard to put down.
GuideWhatIsMoba.pageTitle: Five Years Deep in the MOBA Rabbit Hole
GuideWhatIsMoba.author: By HUB-GAME
leadParagraphs: Up front: a MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) is not a game I would cheerfully hand to just anyone with a "trust me, it's fun, give it a shot."

I still remember my first day in the genre. A friend talked me into installing it, and I could not tell you what was happening on screen. Some ability I never saw coming landed on me from somewhere off to the side, everything went grey, and a teammate typed: please just stay under the tower.
I uninstalled it that same night, fully convinced the whole thing was unfair garbage.
GuideWhatIsMoba.pullQuote: And then, a few days later, it surfaced out of nowhere: if I hadn't walked through that bush, I probably would have lived. I was clicking download again before I had really decided to.
GuideWhatIsMoba.leadOutro: That was the start of everything. I'm past 2,000 hours in the genre now. So here is my attempt to work out, from my own experience, why these games swallow so much of your time.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section1Heading: ■ Fifteen to twenty minutes a match, and the perfect high only lands once every ten
section1Setup: A MOBA match is five players against five, all tangled up on the same map. Everyone opens at level 1, farms minions for gold, and buys items to grow into the late game.

The correct play changes with every situation, and plenty of matches fall apart purely because nobody on the team is reading it the same way. Eight games out of ten I close the client annoyed, still stinging, still wondering why nobody rotated when I pinged.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section1Highlight: But in the other one or two, you get the impossible moment.
section1Payoff: Late game, the match already looking lost, no vision anywhere on the map, and the teamfight timing lands exactly right. Their main damage dealer goes down in the opening second, the ace follows, and a dead game flips.

The shaking hands and the rush that hits right after aren't something I've found in any action game or FPS. Once you've had that once, the eight losses stop reading as losses and turn into the setup for the next one. That, I think, is the genuinely dangerous part of this genre.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Heading: ■ Five roles, and one of them will fit you
GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Intro: The same way soccer has strikers and keepers, a MOBA team is built out of five roles.

roles.name: TOP:
roles.description: The far edge of the map, where you and your lane opponent trade blows for as long as it takes. It suits patient players who like a straight 1v1.

roles.name: MID:
roles.description: The center of the map, usually on a flashy assassin or mage. Made for players who want the spotlight and hold up under pressure.

roles.name: JUNGLE:
roles.description: No lane of your own. You clear the camps in the forest and look for gank windows. The role for people who like reading the whole map at once.

roles.name: ADC (Marksman):
roles.description: Weak in the early game, but once the gold is banked, you can shred the enemy team on auto-attacks alone. The team's main damage source in the late game.

roles.name: SUPPORT:
roles.description: Heals, shields, and vision for the rest of the team. It looks unglamorous, but the support is usually the one who decides when a teamfight starts.

GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Outro: Even if you start out sure your reflexes aren't good enough, you can still decide games from the jungle or by specializing on support. Finding the role that matches how your head already works is a real part of the appeal.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section3Heading: ■ Last thing, for anyone about to start
section3Paragraphs: If you're thinking about picking up a MOBA, I'd strongly suggest either muting team chat or queuing with a friend for the first stretch. There is an enormous amount to learn, and you are going to get rolled while you learn it.
But once you're through that first wall and you land the combo exactly the way you pictured it, you'll arrive at the same thought I did: oh no, this game has me.
GuideWhatIsMoba.ctaCompare: Compare: Honor of Kings vs. Wild Rift, which one suits you?

definitionBlock.heading: What a MOBA is, in one minute
paragraphs: A MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) is a competitive genre in which two teams of five fight over a single map. Each player controls one character, earns gold, and buys items to grow stronger as the match goes on. The first team to destroy the enemy base (the Nexus, or the Crystal in Honor of Kings) wins. The major titles are all free-to-play.
Match length depends on the game. In our comparison article, Honor of Kings matches run about 10 to 15 minutes and Wild Rift matches about 15 to 20.

On PC, the genre is defined by League of Legends (2009) and Dota 2 (2013). On mobile, the two we cover here are Honor of Kings and League of Legends: Wild Rift; Arena of Valor and Pokémon UNITE belong to the same genre.

GuideHOK.title: Why We Recommend Honor of Kings: A Thrilling 15-Minute MOBA
GuideHOK.intro: Six months on the global version, from a longtime PC MOBA player. Ultimates unlock in under two minutes and games end in 10 to 15, and that same pace is why an early lead tends to snowball.
GuideHOK.heading: Six Months of Honor of Kings: My Honest Take on the MOBA That Fits After Work
GuideHOK.author: Written by HUB-GAME
leadParagraphs: I have played MOBAs on PC for years, and I walked into this one carrying a bias: a MOBA on a phone means a cramped screen and mushy controls, right?

Then the global version of Honor of Kings reached Japan on June 20, 2024, I gave it a shot, and that bias did not survive the first session. Six months later I still catch myself queuing up "just one more" after work with my brain running on fumes. Here is my honest take on why the pacing works so well.
GuideHOK.tempoHeading: ■ 10 to 15 minutes a match, with no dead air
tempoParagraphs: The pace is the first thing that got me.

In a PC MOBA, the opening ten minutes are usually a patience test: you and your lane opponent quietly last-hitting minions and trading poke. In HoK you hit level 4 in under two minutes and everyone has their ultimate unlocked (as of the August 2026 build).

Movement speed and farming income are tuned to match, so a fight is breaking out somewhere on the map almost from the first minute. There is no lull to sit through, and 10 to 15 minutes is usually enough for one team to push through the towers and close it out.
If you cannot give up 30-plus minutes on a weeknight but still want the tension of a real competitive match, the format lines up with a working adult's schedule almost uncomfortably well.
GuideHOK.controlsHeading: ■ Touch controls that stay out of the way
controlsParagraphs: It is a virtual stick on a phone screen, but the inputs stick where you put them and the response is quick.

Skill aiming is assisted just enough that combos go off in the direction you intended without the game feeling like it is playing for you. It clicks hardest on assassins and mages: dashing behind a squishy target and dumping a full burst combo on them lands closer to an action game than to lane management.

The roster helps too. Heroes drawn from the Three Kingdoms and Chinese mythology — Zhuge Liang, Sun Wukong, Diaochan and the rest — come with loud, colorful spell effects, and simply moving them around the map is satisfying on its own.
downsideParagraphs: It would not be a fair review if I only listed the good parts.

Because matches move fast and gold comes in quickly, the team that builds an early lead tends to snowball straight through to the base. If what you enjoy is the heavier macro game — holding under tower, controlling the map and grinding out a comeback — HoK can feel blunt by comparison.
verdictList: 116 heroes as of 2026-08-26 (Honor of Kings Hub data). Fighters (38) and Mages (37) make up the bulk of the roster, while Tanks (17) and Supports (16) are the thinnest roles.

Patches land every two weeks. The last three hit on July 16, July 30 and August 13, 2026, exactly 14 days apart. The shop holds 114 items, and there are 30 Arcana, ten each in red, blue and green (as of 2026-08-26).

The match runs on a fixed clock. Outer towers take 40% reduced damage for the first four minutes, the Overlord spawns at 2:00, the Tyrant at 4:00, and the Tempest Dragon at 20:00. Most games finish well before that, and 20 minutes is about the ceiling (Honor of Kings Hub beginner guide, checked 2026-08-26).
GuideHOK.closing: For the finer points of who it suits and who it doesn't, see the comparison article, where it sits side by side with Wild Rift.
GuideHOK.cta: See tier lists and builds on Honor of Kings Hub

GuideWildRift.title: Wild Rift: Depth and Competitiveness on Mobile
GuideWildRift.intro: A review from someone who spent years on League of Legends on PC. Wild Rift kept warding and last-hitting intact; the price is 15-to-20-minute matches and a lot to learn before you're comfortable.
GuideWildRift.heading: No Compromises: Why Wild Rift Doesn't Play Like a Mobile Game
GuideWildRift.author: Written by HUB-GAME
lead: As someone who spent years on League of Legends on PC, I met the announcement of League of Legends: Wild Rift with equal parts excitement and dread.

There was no way a phone screen could carry League's macro game or the precision that its harder champions demand — that was my assumption going in. Then I actually played it, and what I found was a Summoner's Rift built without shortcuts.
GuideWildRift.section1Heading: ■ Warding and last-hitting made the cut
section1Body: When a MOBA gets streamlined for mobile, the fiddly parts are usually the first to go: wards and vision control disappear, and last-hitting gets automated or flattened into passive gold income.
Wild Rift kept both. Choosing where to drop a ward, and reading when the enemy jungler is about to come out of the fog, is the same mind game it is on PC.

Last-hitting matters just as much — miss the CS and you simply don't get the gold — so every step forward to harass and every step back to hold your spacing in lane still carries weight. That strictness is where the depth comes from, and it's exactly the part other mobile MOBAs tend to sand off.
GuideWildRift.section2Heading: ■ The payoff when your mechanics turn a fight around
section2Body: The controls weren't dumbed down either. The high-skill champions are still genuinely hard to play, and the gap between knowing a combo and landing it is as wide as ever.
Yasuo's dash chains, Zed's shadow-swap combos, Lee Sin's Insec (ward-hop into a Flash kick) — they all made it over, and what your fingers can do translates directly into results.
Sitting on a sliver of HP, dodging a skillshot you saw coming, then Flashing into a combo to turn the kill around: that's a win you know you earned rather than one the game handed you.
GuideWildRift.section3Heading: ■ The honest downsides: a lot to learn, and matches aren't short
section3Body: The flip side of that authenticity is a steep wall for newcomers.

A game usually runs 15 to 20 minutes, and you can't walk away mid-match without leaving four teammates a man down. On top of that there's a mountain to memorize: item builds, what every champion's abilities actually do, and which Dragon buffs your team is stacking.
If you're looking for something you can tap through with half your attention, this probably isn't it.
recommendedFor: 141 champions as of 2026-08-26 (Wild Rift Hub). Six roles — Fighter, Tank, Mage, Assassin, Marksman and Support — spread across five positions: Top (Solo), Jungle, Mid, Duo (ADC) and Support.

Patches arrive roughly every two weeks. Patch 7.2 landed on July 8, 2026, 7.2a followed a week later on July 15, and 7.2b (July 29), 7.2c (August 12) and 7.2d (August 26) came at 14-day intervals (Riot's official patch notes, checked 2026-08-26). Wild Rift Hub's data reflects patches through 7.2c (updated 2026-08-12).

The tier list has six tiers, OP through D, broken out by all five positions, with four rank brackets to choose from: Diamond+, Master+, Challenger and Rift Apex. It is built on the Chinese server's official statistics for Master and above, as of 2026-08-20.
GuideWildRift.conclusion: To see whether Wild Rift or Honor of Kings is the better fit for you, read the comparison article, where the two are lined up side by side.
GuideWildRift.ctaLabel: Browse champion guides on Wild Rift Hub

GuideCompare.title: Honor of Kings vs Wild Rift: Which Mobile MOBA Suits You?
GuideCompare.intro: Tempo, vision, and how buying items works: the differences that matter, from someone who has put hours into both. Honor of Kings runs 10 to 15 minutes a game and Wild Rift 15 to 20. Here is how to choose.
GuideCompare.heading: Honor of Kings or Wild Rift? An Honest Take on Which One to Play
GuideCompare.lead: Honor of Kings (HoK) and League of Legends: Wild Rift are the two heavyweights of mobile MOBA. If you are stuck on which one to start with, here is a straight answer from someone who has put serious hours into both.

hok.label: Fast, high-tempo matches
hok.name: Honor of Kings
hok.body: Matches run 10 to 15 minutes. The pace is quick and teamfights break out early. It leans hard into momentum, which suits players who want a short, satisfying session and newcomers easing into the genre.

wr.label: Deep macro and competition
wr.name: Wild Rift
wr.body: Matches run 15 to 20 minutes. Ward placement and vision control, tight last-hitting, precise mechanics. It is built for players who want PC-style strategic depth and a high skill ceiling.

section1.heading: ■ 1. The Real Split: Match Tempo and Vision
section1.intro: The two biggest differences are match length and tempo and whether wards and vision control exist at all.
section1.hokBody: There is no ward war, so enemy positions on the map stay relatively readable. Movement and farming are fast, and a full teamfight can break out two or three minutes in. The design skips the setup phase and gets straight to fighting.
section1.wrBody: Fog of war is in play, so placing wards to hold vision is not optional. That gives you the tension of never quite knowing where the enemy will collapse from, plus the macro payoff of reading them and getting there first.

section2.heading: ■ 2. How Item Buying and Recall Work
section2.hokBody: You can buy items anywhere on the map without recalling. Unless you are one hit from dying, there is no reason to head back, so the game keeps rolling without the usual dead time.
section2.wrBody: Buying items means recalling all the way to the fountain. You have to read the lane state and pick your moment to reset and upgrade, and that timing decision carries real strategic weight.

section3.heading: ■ 3. Side by Side, From a Player Perspective

tableRows.hok: Anywhere on the map (keeps the pace up)

tableRows.wr: Western dark fantasy, the LoL universe

tableRows.hok: 116 heroes across six roles: Tank, Fighter, Assassin, Mage, Marksman and Support. 33 of them are listed under two roles.
tableRows.wr: 141 champions across the same six roles: Fighter, Tank, Mage, Assassin, Marksman and Support.

tableRows.hok: Five: Clash Lane (solo), Jungle, Mid Lane, Farm Lane and Roam. The roamer has no lane of their own and moves across the whole map.
tableRows.wr: Five: Top (Baron Lane), Jungle, Mid, Duo (Dragon Lane) and Support. Top and Duo sometimes swap lanes after the first turret falls or to set up for an upcoming objective.

tableRows.hok: 114 items in six categories (physical, magic, defense, movement, jungle, roam), with six slots. Every tier-2 boot costs 700G.
tableRows.wr: 167 items including 16 boots. Non-boot items split by price into 12 basic, 43 mid-tier and 96 core, topping out at 3,400G. Six slots, and only one item with an active effect.

tableRows.hok: 30 Arcana, 10 each in red, blue and green. You fill 10 slots per color, 30 in total, and level each one from 1 to 5, where the big jump comes at level 5.
tableRows.wr: 53 runes in four trees (Domination, Precision, Resolve, Sorcery): 13 keystones plus 40 minor runes.

tableRows.hok: 11 spells with 30-120s cooldowns, unlocked by account level: Sprint at level 1, Flash not until level 19. Jungle items require Smite.
tableRows.wr: 9 spells with 10-150s cooldowns. Smite is the shortest at 10s; Flash and Teleport the longest at 150s. Smite upgrades to Chill Smite after three uses.

tableRows.hok: Overlord spawns at 2:00 and Tyrant at 4:00. From 10:00 their Shadow versions take over, and the Tempest Dragon appears at 20:00 with a team-wide shield.
tableRows.wr: Four elemental dragons (Infernal, Ocean, Mountain, Cloud), Rift Herald, Baron Nashor and the late-game Elder Dragon.

tableRows.hok: Roughly every two weeks. In July and August 2026 the updates landed on Jul 2, 16 and 30 and Aug 13, 14 days apart. The Season 15 "Grand Venture" update on Jun 17 added four heroes at once.
tableRows.wr: Roughly every two weeks. After 7.2 on Jul 8, patches 7.2a-7.2d followed on Jul 15, Jul 29, Aug 12 and Aug 26. Numbered patches are about three months apart (7.1 on Apr 7, 7.2 on Jul 8); ranked Season 21 opened Apr 10.

tableRows.hok: Developed by TiMi Studio Group, published by Level Infinite (Tencent Games). The global version launched in Japan, North America and Europe on June 20, 2024.
tableRows.wr: Riot Games. Open beta began on October 27, 2020 in Japan, South Korea and Southeast Asia.

tableRows.hok: 819.1 MB, iOS 12.0 or later. Also on Google Play for Android.
tableRows.wr: 1.1 GB, iOS 15.0 or later. Also on Google Play for Android.

section4.heading: ■ 4. Verdict: Which One Is for You

recommendHok.heading: ▶ Who Honor of Kings Is For
points: • Players with limited free time who want a match wrapped up in 10 to 15 minutes
• Anyone who wants flashy combos and kills without a pile of homework first
• MOBA newcomers who want to pick up the fundamentals while still having fun

recommendWr.heading: ▶ Who Wild Rift Is For
points: • Players who want PC-level tactics and mind games
• Competitive players who want precise skill dodging and vision control to decide the game
• Anyone drawn to the League of Legends world and champion designs

GuideCompare.tableFootnote: Figures are as of August 26, 2026. Hero, item, arcana and spell counts come from the data published on each strategy site; patch dates are the publication dates of each game’s official patch notes; app size and OS requirements are as shown on the Japanese App Store.

Quiz.title: Mobile MOBA Aptitude Quiz
Quiz.subtitle: Answer 5 quick questions and we'll suggest the MOBA that matches your playstyle — plus the role you should main!
Quiz.q1: What match tempo do you prefer?
Quiz.q1a1: Fast 10-15 minute games with constant action!
Quiz.q1a2: Slower 15-20 minute games with farming and strategy!
Quiz.q2: How do you like your controls and combat?
Quiz.q2a2: Precise play with vision control and skill dodging!
Quiz.q3: Which art style appeals to you?
Quiz.q3a1: Vibrant Eastern fantasy and historical heroes!
Quiz.q4: Where on the map do you want to be fighting?
Quiz.q4a1: On the front line, soaking the enemy's damage so my team can go in
Quiz.q4a2: In the middle, a short walk from every lane so I can dictate the pace
Quiz.q4a3: Nowhere near a lane — roaming the jungle and the enemy's half of the map
Quiz.q4a4: Safe in the backline, dealing damage without getting touched
Quiz.q4a5: Right next to a teammate, warding and peeling for them
Quiz.q5: Which kind of win feels best to you?
Quiz.q5a1: Completely shutting down your lane opponent 1v1
Quiz.q5a2: Reading the enemy's next move and collapsing on them first
Quiz.q5a3: Deleting two or three enemies in a single teamfight
Quiz.q5a4: Finishing the game at the top of the damage chart
Quiz.q5a5: Setting your team up so they can commit without hesitating
Quiz.resultHokDesc: 10 to 15 minutes per match. Enjoy fast-paced games and flashy skill combos.
Quiz.resultWrDesc: Vision control with wards and deep laning. Great for players who want to hone real skill.
Quiz.role_hok_top_desc: The clash lane is the island lane: long 1v1s with almost no help, then leading the engage and eating the enemy's opening spells in teamfights. Your answers lean toward handling a situation on your own, and clash is the role that lets you decide when the fight starts.
Quiz.role_wr_top_desc: Top is the island lane: long 1v1s with almost no help, then leading the engage and eating the enemy's opening spells in teamfights. Your answers lean toward handling a situation on your own, and top is the role that lets you decide when the fight starts.
Quiz.role_hok_jungle_desc: Junglers skip laning entirely — you clear camps and pick your own timings for ganks and objectives. You said you win by reading the enemy and hitting first, and jungle is the one role that gets to choose where the fight happens. Jungle items require Smite, and they cut your damage to minions by 25% until the 10:00 mark.
Quiz.role_wr_jungle_desc: Junglers skip laning entirely — you clear camps and pick your own timings for ganks and objectives. You said you win by reading the enemy and hitting first, and jungle is the one role that gets to choose where the fight happens.
Quiz.role_hok_mid_desc: Mid is the shortest walk to every other lane, so you provide damage while setting the tempo of the game. You picked quick, decisive fights and staying involved across the map, which is exactly what mid does once the wave is shoved.
Quiz.role_wr_mid_desc: Mid is the shortest walk to every other lane, so you provide damage while setting the tempo of the game. You picked quick, decisive fights and staying involved across the map, which is exactly what mid does once the wave is shoved.
Quiz.role_hok_adc_desc: Marksmen turn CS into gold and gold into steady damage from the safety of the backline. You chose to farm up and win on raw output, and that patient early game is what the farm lane is trading for. Honor of Kings lets you shop from anywhere, so you can stay in lane for it.
Quiz.role_wr_adc_desc: Marksmen turn last hits (CS) into gold and gold into steady damage from the safety of the backline. You chose to farm up and win on raw output, and that patient early game is what an ADC is trading for.
Quiz.role_hok_support_desc: A roamer buys the Knowledge Gem first, moves across the whole map, soaks the damage meant for the carry and locks enemies down so teammates can commit. You put your team's survival and map information ahead of your own kill count. Honor of Kings has no wards, so vision comes from firing a skill into a bush and watching for a reaction.
Quiz.role_wr_support_desc: Supports buy the wards, take the damage meant for the carry, and lock enemies down so teammates can commit. You put your team's survival and map information ahead of your own kill count, which is the entire job description.

Glossary.title: Essential MOBA Glossary
Glossary.description: The basic terms every beginner should know — the shared language of MOBA players.
Glossary.pageLead: Not sure what a gank is, or what CS actually stands for? These are the terms Wild Rift and Honor of Kings players use in chat, in guides and in ranked — defined the way they are actually used, with the differences between the two games noted where they matter.

Gank.def: Ambushing an enemy from another lane or the jungle to create a numbers advantage. A jungler's main job.

Laning.def: The early phase of the game where you kill minions in your lane to earn experience and gold.
Laning.note: The lanes go by different names. Wild Rift has Top (Baron lane), Mid and Duo (Dragon lane); Honor of Kings has the Clash Lane (top), Mid and the Farm Lane (bottom).

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (lane roles)
Wild Rift Hub: Beginner Guide (lane roles)

LastHit.def: Dealing the killing blow to a minion to earn gold. The foundation of income — accuracy translates directly into item advantages.
LastHit.note: In Honor of Kings a last hit pays roughly 1.5x what a minion dying next to you does, and you can spend that gold from anywhere on the map. On the Wild Rift side, read it together with the eight wave-management entries in the glossary — freezing, slow pushing and the rest.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (last hitting)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (wave management)

Build.def: The order in which you buy items and level skills. Adapting your build to the enemy team is key to winning.
Build.note: Wild Rift has 167 items plus 53 runes; Honor of Kings has 114 items plus 30 arcana. Boots differ too: Wild Rift upgrades them in tiers from a 400-gold pair, while every upper-tier boot in Honor of Kings costs a flat 700 gold and can be swapped for free after a five-minute cooldown.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Item Build Simulator
Wild Rift Hub: Items

BuffDebuff.def: Buffs strengthen (e.g. attack up) and debuffs weaken (e.g. slows). Jungle monster buffs are crucial for early-game control.
BuffDebuff.note: In Honor of Kings, Red Buff adds a slow and true damage over time, Blue Buff gives 20% cooldown reduction and mana regen, and both respawn every 90 seconds. In Wild Rift the big team-wide buffs come from the four dragons.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (Red & Blue Buffs)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (the four dragons)

KDA.def: Your kill/death/assist ratio. Beginners improve fastest by focusing on dying less.

Carry.def: The hero your team feeds gold and safe farm so they can win late-game fights. If you are the carry, take the free farm; if you are not, play around protecting the one who is.

Tank.def: A high-health frontliner who starts fights and soaks damage. Tanks buy resistances instead of damage, so judge them by how much enemy attention they pull, not by KDA.

Fighter.def: A durable melee hero who still deals real damage — able to keep trading in a fight without being a pure tank. Usually takes the solo lane: Top in Wild Rift, the Clash Lane in Honor of Kings.
Fighter.note: Their home is Top (Baron lane) in Wild Rift and the Clash Lane (top side) in Honor of Kings. Both are 1v1 lanes; in teamfights a fighter either holds the frontline or flanks into the enemy backline.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Clash Lane Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List (Top)

Assassin.def: A burst hero built to reach the enemy carry and delete them in one combo. Strong when the enemy is split up, near-useless when they group and peel for each other.

Mage.def: A ranged magic-damage hero, usually in the mid lane. Mages jump in strength the moment their first major item completes, so it is worth checking the enemy mage's build before you fight.

Marksman.def: A ranged basic-attack carry who scales with items. Wild Rift plays them in the Duo lane (Dragon lane) with a support. Honor of Kings puts them in the Farm Lane (bottom). The roamer holds no lane and moves across the whole map, so a partner is not always standing beside you.
Marksman.note: A Wild Rift ADC farms with a support standing guard. In Honor of Kings the roamer holds no lane: it helps clear the first mid wave at level 1, then moves on to take vision around the boss pits, so the Farm Lane marksman cannot count on a partner standing next to them.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Farm Lane Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List (Duo)

Support.def: The role that gives up farm in exchange for vision, crowd control and peel. In Wild Rift the support starts beside the marksman and also manages wards. Honor of Kings calls the role Roam: it holds no lane, moves across the whole map, and — with no ward item — earns its keep by checking bushes, protecting teammates and calling the start of a fight.
Support.note: A Wild Rift support pairs with the ADC in the Duo lane and handles wards. The equivalent Honor of Kings role is the Roam, which buys the 300-gold Knowledge Gem and moves across the whole map instead of holding a lane.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Roam Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Beginner Guide (support role)

Jungler.def: The player who farms neutral camps instead of a lane and decides where to gank. Their pathing sets the early tempo for the whole team.
Jungler.note: Smite is a different spell in each game. Honor of Kings: 1,500 true damage on a 30-second cooldown, and you cannot buy jungle items without it. Wild Rift: 600 true damage on a 10-second cooldown, upgrading to Chill Smite after three uses.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Summoner Spells (Smite)
Wild Rift Hub: Summoner Spells

Minion.def: The AI soldiers that march down each lane. They are your steady income — clearing waves pays for your build, and shoving them into a tower is how you take it down.
Minion.note: Honor of Kings waves gain a long-range ballista from 4:00, and killing the Overlord turns your next two waves into Dragon Vanguards. In Wild Rift it is the Baron buff that supercharges nearby minions.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Jungle Boss Guide (Overlord)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Baron Nashor)

Recall.def: Channeling back to your fountain to heal and shop. Time it right after you shove the wave in, so you lose the least gold and experience while you are away.
Recall.note: Honor of Kings lets you buy items from anywhere on the map, so a recall is for healing, not shopping. In Wild Rift the usual timing is right before a cannon minion wave arrives or straight after crashing your wave into the tower.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (buy anywhere)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (recall timing)

Farm.def: Steadily collecting gold and experience from minions and jungle camps. When a fight is not clearly winnable, taking a wave is usually the higher-value play.

Jungle.def: The neutral area between lanes. Defeat monsters there for experience and buffs.

Bush.def: Grass that hides you from enemy view. A classic spot to ambush the enemy carry.

Tower.def: Lane defenses that hit hard and switch to you the moment you attack an enemy hero in range. Only step in when your own minion wave is there to take the shots for you.
Tower.note: In Honor of Kings, outer towers take 40% less damage for the first four minutes, and hitting a tower with no allied minions nearby cuts your damage by 55%. Wild Rift's early tower plan is to take the Rift Herald and send it charging in.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (tower protection)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Rift Herald)

Nexus.def: The final structure in the enemy base — the Nexus in Wild Rift, the Crystal in Honor of Kings. Destroying it ends the match regardless of the kill score.
Nexus.note: In Honor of Kings the Crystal cannot be attacked until at least one high ground tower is down. In Wild Rift, breaking a lane's third tower — the Inhibitor Turret — spawns Super Minions in that lane.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (high ground towers)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Inhibitor Turret)

Ward.def: A placeable item that reveals part of the map. Wild Rift gives every player free wards from the shop, while Honor of Kings has no ward item at all — there, vision comes from bushes, the minimap and hero skills.
Ward.note: Wild Rift vision runs on wards, cleared with the Sweeping Lens, and wards even serve as Teleport targets. Honor of Kings has no ward at all — the roamer walks into the bush first to check it.

links.label: Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (vision & Sweeping Lens)
Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (vision & bushes)

FogOfWar.def: The unlit part of the map where enemies are invisible to you. When an enemy disappears from the minimap, assume they are walking toward you until you see otherwise.

Fountain.def: The healing zone in your base where you shop and refill. Enemies who chase you into it get shredded by the fountain's attack, so a fountain dive is almost never worth it.

Ace.def: Wiping out the entire enemy team. Use the window to take towers and objectives and swing the game.

Peel.def: Protecting your carry (damage dealer) from enemy attacks.

CC.def: Any effect that takes control away from a hero — stun, knock-up, root, silence, slow. Chaining CC is how a team kills a tank, and holding your escape until after the first CC lands is how you survive one.
CC.note: The cleanse spell is Purify in Honor of Kings (120s cooldown) and Cleanse in Wild Rift (110s). In both games, suppression is the one effect the usual cleanses cannot remove.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Summoner Spells (Purify)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (14 crowd-control effects)

Burst.def: Damage delivered in one short combo rather than over time. Burst heroes live or die on whether the target dies before it can react, so they need setup or CC to land it.

Poke.def: Chipping away at enemy health from outside their range before a fight starts. Enough poke forces the enemy to recall or fight at a health deficit.

Sustain.def: Health you recover on your own — lifesteal, regeneration, or a heal skill. Good sustain lets you stay in lane through poke instead of giving up waves to recall.

Dive.def: Attacking an enemy who is standing under their own tower. It only works when you have a minion wave to hold the tower's aggro and enough damage to finish before it kills you.
Dive.note: Honor of Kings towers take 40% reduced damage until 4:00, so dives before then almost never work. The Wild Rift glossary covers tower aggro swapping — passing the tower's target from one teammate to the next so everyone walks out.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (tower protection)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (tower dive & aggro swap)

Focus.def: Agreeing on one target and killing it first. Damage spread across five enemies kills nobody; five players hitting the same squishy usually decides the fight on the spot.

Kiting.def: Moving between basic attacks so you keep dealing damage while staying out of reach. Attack, step back, attack again — it is the core mechanic of every marksman.

Engage.def: Engage is the skill that starts a fight — a knock-up, a hook, a dash in. Disengage is what pulls your team out of a bad one. Whichever side has the better engage usually gets to choose when the fight happens.

Snowball.def: Turning a small lead into an ever-growing advantage and keeping control of the game.

Push.def: Killing minions to move the front line toward the enemy's towers.

Macro.def: Big-picture strategy: map awareness, objective control, and rotations. Its counterpart, micro, refers to mechanical skill.

Objective.def: Neutral monsters that grant powerful team-wide buffs — Wild Rift's dragons and Baron, Honor of Kings' Tyrant and Overlord. Teamfights around them often decide the game.
Objective.note: Honor of Kings objectives run on a clock: Overlord at 2:00, Tyrant at 4:00, their Shadow versions at 10:00 and the Tempest Dragon at 20:00. Wild Rift has seven — four dragons, the Rift Herald, Baron Nashor and the Elder Dragon.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Jungle Boss Guide (Tyrant & Overlord)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (all 7 objectives)

Roam.def: Leaving your lane to make something happen elsewhere — a gank, an objective, a vision sweep. Roam after you shove your wave in, so the trip does not cost you farm. In Honor of Kings, Roam is also the name of the support position.
Roam.note: In Honor of Kings, Roam is also the name of a role, with its own tier list. The roamer helps clear the first mid wave at level 1, then goes to take vision around the boss pits. In Wild Rift the word only describes the action.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Roam Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Roam)

SplitPush.def: Pushing a side lane alone while your team holds the enemy's attention elsewhere. It forces them to send someone to answer, which is how you create the numbers fight your team can win.
SplitPush.note: Honor of Kings speeds up the Clash Lane side with a warp point — kill its sprite to activate it, then it has a 30-second cooldown. The Wild Rift glossary lays out the 1-4 and 1-3-1 formations.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (warp point)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (1-4 and 1-3-1 split push)

WaveManagement.def: Controlling where the minion waves meet. Freeze the wave near your own tower to farm safely, or slow push a big wave first so you have time to take an objective.

Scaling.def: How much stronger a hero gets from levels and items. A late-scaling team should trade early aggression for farm; an early-game team has to convert its lead before the other side catches up.

PowerSpike.def: The moment a hero jumps in strength — a key level or a completed item. Look for fights right after your own spike, and avoid them right after the enemy's.
PowerSpike.note: In Honor of Kings the first spike is level 4, when your ultimate unlocks. In Wild Rift, tier 3 boots only unlock at 10:00, so the pair you buy early decides the passive you finish the game with.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (game flow)
Wild Rift Hub: Items (boots)

Meta.def: The heroes, builds and strategies that are strongest under the current patch. It shifts with every balance change, so check the patch date on any tier list you read.
Meta.note: The two tier lists draw on different data. Honor of Kings Hub uses win, pick and ban rates from the official in-game HoK Camp; Wild Rift Hub uses official China-server stats from Master rank and above.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List

About.title: About
About.siteText: HUB-GAME (hub-game.com) is a strategy portal focused on mobile MOBAs. This site offers comparison articles, an aptitude quiz, and a glossary to help you choose a title, while our sister sites cover detailed strategy for Wild Rift and Honor of Kings.
About.operatorText: HUB-GAME team (email: contact@hub-game.com / X: @hub_gamecom). The articles and data are produced by an operator who plays Wild Rift and Honor of Kings daily, working from hands-on play and the actual in-game screens.
About.policyText: Articles are based on what we have verified through actual play. Because patches make information go stale, we note the verification date for numbers and balance claims wherever possible. Anything we cannot confirm is marked as unverified rather than guessed. If you spot an error, please let us know via the contact page.
About.contactText: For questions, information, or feedback about our content, please see the contact page.
methodList: Hero base stats and skill numbers are transcribed from screenshots of the actual game screens. For Honor of Kings, we cross-checked 113 hero stat screens plus 140 skill and item detail screens in August 2026.

Win, pick, and ban rates on the tier lists come from official statistics (HoK Camp for Honor of Kings), fetched manually, with the retrieval date shown on the page. They are not always current, so check the date before you rely on them.
Before publishing, the Japanese and English data sets are compared mechanically so that an outdated value cannot survive in only one language.
Where the comparison article or the glossary describes how the two games differ, the figures are the same ones published on each strategy site, with the verification date attached.

GuideTermMapping.title: Honor of Kings ⇄ Wild Rift: Term Map and Switching Guide
GuideTermMapping.intro: Twenty-two things Honor of Kings and Wild Rift both have but call by different names, lined up side by side — each with a one-line note on how the mechanics actually differ, from spawn timers to where you are allowed to shop.
GuideTermMapping.lead: Crystal and Nexus, Tyrant and Dragon, Arcana and Runes. The names differ, but the job each one does in a match is close to identical. Treat them as the same thing, though, and the details — spawn times, how shopping works — will trip you up. Drawing on the glossaries of our two strategy sites, this page pairs up the terms and notes where the mechanics diverge.

sections.heading: Map and Base
sections.intro: Both maps run three lanes plus a jungle. What changes is what the base is called and how the lanes are named.

rows.note: Destroying it ends the game in both. In HoK you must bring down at least one high ground tower before the Crystal can be attacked.
Both spawn Super Minions in that lane once destroyed. In Wild Rift this is the third turret standing just outside the base.

rows.wr: Baron Lane (listed as "Top" on Wild Rift Hub)
rows.note: A fighter or tank 1v1 in both games. In HoK, kill the sprite at the nearby warp point early so the teleport is ready when you need it.

rows.wr: Dragon Lane ("Duo" on Wild Rift Hub)
rows.note: Marksman plus support in both. HoK adds a gold object in the middle of the lane that pays the whole team when destroyed.
Every Wild Rift player carries a free ward, and where you place it is a mind game. HoK has no wards: throw a skill into the bush and watch for a hit.

sections.heading: Objectives and Buffs
sections.intro: HoK's bosses spawn early on fixed timers; Wild Rift revolves around a rotating set of elemental dragons. Even when a boss plays the same role, the reward takes a different shape.

rows.note: Tyrant spawns at 4:00 and gives everyone Chain Lightning on their attacks. Wild Rift's dragons each buff a different team-wide stat depending on the element.
Overlord spawns at 2:00 and turns your next two waves into Dragon Vanguards. Herald spawns at 6:00 and drops the Eye of the Herald, which sends it charging into a turret.
At 10:00 both HoK bosses are replaced by their Shadow versions. Baron appears from the mid game on and grants Hand of Baron: more AD/AP and heavily empowered nearby minions.
Tempest spawns at 20:00 and shields every living teammate for 20–50% of max HP. Elder makes your attacks execute enemies below a health threshold.

sections.heading: Progression: Items, Arcana/Runes, Spells
sections.intro: Pre-game setup follows different logic in Arcana and Runes, and once the match starts the biggest gap is where you are allowed to shop.

rows.note: Arcana are fixed bonuses slotted 10 each in red, blue and green, 30 in total. Runes come from four trees — Domination, Precision, Resolve, Sorcery — as a keystone plus minor runes.

rows.concept: Shared skills picked before the match
rows.hok: Battle Spells (Summoner Spells on the HoK Hub list page)
rows.note: HoK has 11, unlocked by account level; Wild Rift has 9. A shared name does not mean shared numbers — the next three rows are examples.
HoK's Flash unlocks at account level 19. Until then, Sprint, available from level 1, fills the same role.
HoK's Smite deals 1,500 true damage plus a 1-second stun, and you cannot buy jungle items without it. Wild Rift's deals 600 true damage and heals you when used on a monster.
Execute deals instant true damage equal to 16% of the target's missing health. Ignite is 5 seconds of true damage over time with Grievous Wounds, used for early kill pressure.
In HoK, any pair you own can be swapped for a different pair for free after a 5-minute cooldown. In Wild Rift you upgrade the 400G Boots of Speed to tier 2, and tier 3 unlocks at 10:00.

sections.heading: Roles and Lanes
sections.intro: HoK calls them heroes and Wild Rift calls them champions, but the five roles are nearly identical. One catch: in HoK, "Roam" is the name of a role, while in Wild Rift it describes an action.

rows.concept: The teammate who enables the others
rows.note: HoK's Roam buys the Knowledge Gem (300G) first and moves across the whole map. Wild Rift's support stands beside the marksman and handles the wards.
Same job. HoK marksmen can shop in lane and rarely need to leave it; in Wild Rift every purchase means a trip back to the fountain.
HoK's jungle items require Smite and cut your damage to minions by 25% until 10:00 in exchange for better rewards from monsters. Wild Rift's jungler is also expected to cover every lane.

sections.heading: Match Flow and Vocabulary
sections.intro: Match length and the level that unlocks your ultimate both differ, so "early game" refers to a different stretch of the clock in each game.

rows.note: In HoK you can buy anywhere, so recalling is mostly about healing. In Wild Rift the shop is fountain-only, and choosing when to go back is a skill in itself.
HoK reaches level 4 in under two minutes and Tempest Dragon at 20:00. In Wild Rift the Rift Herald arrives at 6:00 — the whole early game sits later on the clock.
Level 4 is HoK's first real window to make a play. Wild Rift unlocks the ultimate at level 5 and ranks it up at 9 and 13.
In HoK, landing the killing blow pays roughly 1.5x what a minion dying next to you does. In Wild Rift, missed CS costs most of the gold, and that gap shows up directly in items.

switchGuide.heading: Habits to Fix First When You Switch
hokToWr: If you come from HoK, the first wall is shopping. Your gold piles up, but you cannot spend it where you stand. You have to be at the fountain, so get in the habit of shoving the wave in, then recalling.

Next, wards. HoK has nothing like them, so you will forget to place them at first. Drop one in the river bush before Dragon or Baron spawns, and clear enemy wards with the Sweeping Lens. That alone removes most of the "why do I get ganked every time" feeling.

Your clock needs resetting too. In HoK, 4:00 is when tower protection drops and the first push begins; in Wild Rift the Rift Herald does not show up until 6:00 and your ultimate waits for level 5. Force a fight in the second minute on HoK instinct and you will be brawling without your ultimate.
wrToHok: Coming from Wild Rift, your first job is the opposite: never stop shopping. The moment gold comes in, open the shop — while walking, while dead, wherever you are. Once you think of recall as a heal button rather than a shopping trip, HoK's tempo starts to make sense.

With no wards, get used to checking bushes by throwing a skill in and watching for a hit. When an enemy vanishes from the minimap, assume they are heading your way. With no way to leave vision behind, your pings carry more of the load.

Every objective comes early. Overlord at 2:00, Tyrant at 4:00, and both swap to their Shadow versions at 10:00. Boots cost a flat 700G, and five minutes after buying a pair you can swap to a different one for free, so change them to match your lane opponent.

GuideTermMapping.closing: Figures reflect Honor of Kings Hub as of 2026-08-26 and Wild Rift Hub as of patch 7.2c. Both games shift with every patch, so when in doubt, check each site's glossary and boss guide.
